messages:
maria_sales: Quick heads-up — kicking off a POC with GreenFin (SQ-ACME-2026). They need Canada-only residency for inference + embeddings, but want an EU fallback if Canada pool is saturated. Need ops + security input before we commit on the quote.

sam_infra: Can do a high-level: primary route -> Canada region, failover -> EU region. Need to confirm sub-processor paths (no US egress).

olivia_sec: Important: client requires BYOK for Canada keys and an attestation that no US sub-processors see plaintext. We'll need to check which cloud partners/edge nodes are in-path.

maria_sales: Two quick asks for presales deck / answer doc: 1) definitive list of sub-processors that could touch data during normal and failover flows; 2) sample routing policy snippet we can show the customer; 3) pricing delta for reserved Canada pin + cross-region egress on failover.

sam_infra: I'll pull the sub-processor list. For routing policy sample, this is what we usually show:
```
routing_policy:
  primary_region: ca-central-1
  fallback_regions: [eu-west-1]
  constraints:
    - avoid_subprocessors: [us-east-1, us-central-1]
    - allow_byo_kms: true
    - sticky_sessions: true
```

sam_infra: Note: sticky_sessions mean we keep tenant pinned to Canada when available. Failover will only route if latency/capacity triggers are met.

olivia_sec: BYOK + failover is tricky: if the fallback region can't access the Canada KMS key, we must either: a) replicate keys under customer-managed BYOK in EU (customer preferred), or b) use a separate EU key and document the key-swap/consent. We'll need to capture this in the SQ response.

jake_sales: Pricing question from the buyer: what's the delta for a pinned Canada tenant vs default hosted? And is cross-region egress billed per token on failover?

sam_infra: Pricing notes: pinned Canada reservation = base + regional premium (typically ~30-45% depending on GPU class). Cross-region failover uses egress metering — yes billed per-token for the region that served the request. I'll ask finance for exact ranges; for presales we can show a conservative estimate.

maria_sales: Can someone draft a short runbook snippet for the customer that explains failover behavior + consent steps for BYOK replication? They want it in the security questionnaire (SQ-ACME-2026).

olivia_sec: Draft runbook outline: 1) Normal flow: tenant pinned to CA, data stays in CA. 2) Trigger: sustained capacity loss or maintenance -> automatic failover to EU. 3) BYOK options: replicate keys to EU (customer-managed) OR pre-approve key-swap consent. 4) Audit logs: we provide event records and KMS access logs for any cross-region access. I'll write the paragraph.

ops-bot: [capacity-check] ca-central-1 reserved pool status: 78% utilized, projected 72-88% over next 48h under current forecast.

sam_infra: Ops note — if customer wants strict no-cross-border under any condition, we must offer dedicated Private deployment in CA (requires contract + infra lead time). For POC we can do pinned tenant + documented failover consent.

maria_sales: Perfect. I'll update the presales answers with: routing policy snippet, sub-processor list (once Sam posts), rough pricing ranges, and Olivia's runbook paragraph. Targeting to send SQ response by EOD tomorrow.

sam_infra: Adding task: I'll attach sub-processor inventory and short network path diagram in the follow-up thread.

jake_sales: I'll flag pricing escalation with finance for an exact committed quote.

maria_sales: Thanks everyone :thumbsup: tagging @olivia_sec for the final SQ language and @sam_infra for the sub-processor list.

olivia_sec: Got it, will post SQ text by lunchtime tomorrow.
